news.headline: Marvell Technology Reports Q2 FY2027 Results After Close; AI Custom Silicon Demand in Focus
news.body: Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) released its fiscal Q2 2027 earnings after the market close on August 27, with Wall Street consensus calling for revenue of approximately $2.71 billion — up ~35% year-over-year — and non-GAAP EPS of $0.93. Markets closely watched Q3 guidance, with consensus already pricing in ~$3.03 billion in quarterly revenue, as CEO Matt Murphy had previously flagged "exceptional AI-related bookings" and a significant upward revision to FY2027 and FY2028 revenue outlooks. MRVL shares surged over 190% year-to-date entering the print, driven by its custom silicon and optical interconnect positioning across U.S. hyperscalers, making guidance the pivotal variable. The report serves as a key read-through for AI infrastructure spending momentum following Nvidia's blockbuster results the prior evening.

news.headline: Nvidia Q2 FY27 Revenue Surges 106% YoY to $96.2B, Guides Q3 to $108B
news.body: Nvidia reported fiscal Q2 2027 earnings of $2.22 per share on revenue of $96.2B, topping consensus estimates of $2.09 EPS and $92.2B revenue for a +5.65% EPS surprise and +3.04% revenue beat. Q3 guidance of ~$108B (+89% YoY) exceeded the $104.2B Street consensus. CEO Jensen Huang declared AI has 'reached its inflection point' with demand broadening well beyond a single hyperscaler. The stock saw a muted positive reaction after hours, consistent with a pattern of post-earnings selling despite repeated beats over the prior four quarters.

news.headline: Salesforce Surges 14% After Hours on Agentforce Boom, Raises Full-Year Outlook
news.body: Salesforce reported Q2 FY27 revenue of $11.35B (+11% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $5.90, vastly exceeding the $3.27 consensus estimate, boosted partly by a $2.6B gain on its Anthropic stake. Agentforce AI annualized revenue topped $1.5B, up 240% YoY, and the company raised full-year revenue guidance to $46.1B–$46.4B implying ~11% growth. Free cash flow spiked 81% to $1.10B, well above the $643M consensus. Shares soared ~14% in extended trading, marking a sharp reversal for a stock down 21% year-to-date ahead of the print.

news.headline: CrowdStrike Reports Best Quarter in Company History; Stock Up ~10% After Hours
news.body: CrowdStrike posted Q2 FY27 revenue of $1.47B (vs. $1.44B expected) and adjusted EPS of $0.31 (vs. $0.29 expected), marking its ninth consecutive EPS beat. The company raised full-year FY27 revenue guidance to $5.99B–$6.01B, above the $5.94B consensus, citing AI-driven structural demand for cybersecurity. GAAP net income was positive for the second consecutive quarter and non-GAAP operating margin expanded. Shares jumped ~10% in extended trading as the stock, already up ~68% year-to-date, cleared a key technical resistance level.

news.headline: Abercrombie & Fitch Surges 37% on $100M Tariff Refund, Record Q2 Sales, Raised Outlook
news.body: Abercrombie & Fitch (NYSE: ANF) posted record second-quarter net sales of $1.27 billion, up 5% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of $4.17 — more than doubling the $1.98 analyst consensus — boosted by roughly $100 million in tariff refunds. The stock surged approximately 37% on Wednesday, marking its biggest single-day jump since November 2025, as the company also raised its full-year net sales growth outlook to around 5% and guided for net income per diluted share of $13.10–$13.60. Management announced at least $500 million in share repurchases for fiscal 2026, and the quarter marked the retailer's 15th consecutive period of sales growth. The outsized move lifted the SPDR S&P Retail ETF (XRT) by ~1% and reinforced investor optimism around tariff-refund tailwinds for U.S. apparel retailers.

news.headline: Bank of Korea Delivers Back-to-Back 25bp Hike to 3%, Lifts 2026 Growth Forecast
news.body: The Bank of Korea raised its benchmark seven-day repo rate by 25 basis points to 3.00% on August 27 — its second consecutive hike and the first back-to-back tightening since January 2023 — driven by sticky core inflation at a three-year high of 2.6% and a renewed surge in Seoul housing prices. The 6-1 decision was broadly in line with market expectations but at the hawkish end of a closely divided consensus. The BOK simultaneously upgraded its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 3.3% from 2.6%, crediting the semiconductor-led boom. The KOSPI trimmed early Nvidia-driven gains to +1.5% after the decision, while KTB futures extended losses; markets now price one further 25bp hike in Q1 2027.

news.headline: Nvidia Q2 Revenue More Than Doubles; Asian Chip Stocks Rise on Beat and Guide-Up
news.body: Nvidia reported fiscal Q2 revenue of approximately $92 billion after the August 26 close, beating consensus of $91.9 billion, with Q3 guidance above Wall Street estimates — lifting Nvidia ADRs roughly 4.7% in after-hours trade. Asian supply-chain stocks rose in Thursday's session: SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics gained 2–3%, Kioxia advanced more than 4%, and Taiwan's TSMC also moved higher. Broader Asian markets showed a mixed picture as US PCE inflation data — running at a three-year high of 3.7% — tempered the AI euphoria, with losses recorded in Tokyo, Hong Kong, Sydney, Singapore, and Manila. The print is the most consequential earnings event of the quarter for the region given SK Hynix's role as Nvidia's sole HBM3E supplier and TSMC's foundry dependence.

news.headline: China July Industrial Profit Growth Slows to 11.2%, Weakest Pace of 2026
news.body: Growth in profits at China's major industrial firms decelerated for a third consecutive month in July, rising 11.2% year-on-year versus June's 15.1% gain, the National Bureau of Statistics reported on Thursday. For the January-to-July period, profits are up 17.6%, modestly below the 18.1% pace forecast by Bloomberg Economics, reflecting a cooling economy and softening price gains. The slowdown is a mild headwind for mainland A-share cyclicals and resource names — sectors that had led earlier 2026 gains on China's recovery trade. The CSI 300 had already been trading around 4,580–4,630 heading into the data, with markets also tracking the Nvidia-led tech rally for near-term direction.

news.headline: SK Hynix Breaks Ground on $3.87B Indiana HBM Packaging Plant; Chey-Huang Meeting Eyed
news.body: SK Hynix held a formal groundbreaking ceremony on August 27 (local time) for its advanced semiconductor packaging facility in West Lafayette, Indiana — the company's first US production base for high-bandwidth memory targeting AI applications. SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won and CEO Kwak Noh-jung attended, with market attention focused on a potential meeting between Chey and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang that could signal further US investment commitments. The $3.87 billion facility, backed by up to $450 million in CHIPS Act direct funding and $500 million in loans, targets HBM mass production from H2 2028. The event amplifies the Seoul-to-Indiana AI supply-chain narrative coinciding with Nvidia's earnings beat.
news.source: Korea Herald / Korea JoongAng Daily / The Elec

news.headline: Kioxia Plans $6.3B Iwate Fab3 to Capture AI-Driven NAND Demand
news.body: Memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings plans to build a third production facility at its Kitakami plant in Iwate Prefecture, northern Japan, with investment expected to exceed 1 trillion yen ($6.27 billion), Nikkei reported on Thursday. The new fab will manufacture high-density 3D NAND flash chips designed for the massive storage workflows generated by AI data-centre services. The announcement follows Kioxia's blockbuster Q1 FY2026 results in which operating profit hit roughly 1.27 trillion yen — about 28 times the year-earlier figure — lifting its market cap briefly above Toyota's. Shares of Kioxia (TSE: 285A) rose more than 5% on the session, and Citi said it would view the news as 'somewhat positive' given what it signals about demand visibility through 2029.

news.headline: Trump Renews Threat to Fire Fed's Cook; Gold Spikes on Fed Independence Fears
news.body: Gold spiked to two-week highs near $3,385/oz after the Trump White House renewed its threat to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, citing alleged mortgage fraud — a charge Cook denies and courts have not upheld. The move reignited fears over Fed independence, weakened the US dollar, and lifted market pricing for September rate cuts above 87%. Cook fired back in a letter on August 26, stating there is 'no legal basis' for removal; her lawyers noted the Supreme Court had blocked an earlier attempt. Gold pulled back to the $3,370–80 range as the dollar partially recovered, though the precious metal remains nearly 2% higher on the week with Friday's PCE print now in sharp focus.

news.headline: Grains Surge to Multi-Year Highs: Corn Hits 3-Year High, Soybeans at Contract Record
news.body: December corn futures climbed to $5.36½/bu — a new contract high and the highest nearby-futures price in roughly three years — while November soybeans surged to a contract-high $12.66 and December soybean meal hit a nine-month high of $339.30/ton. The rally was driven by a confluence of US yield concerns, tightening Black Sea export availability amid the ongoing Ukraine war, and fears that cheap grain will no longer be reliably accessible. Wheat joined the move, with the August WASDE having already pegged 2026 US all-wheat production at the lowest since 1970. Markets are now flagging next month's September 11 USDA Supply & Demand report as pivotal for setting price direction through year-end.
news.source: Ag Bull Trading / Farm Progress / ADMISI

news.headline: Oil Slumps ~3% to Near One-Month Low as Iran-Oman Outline Hormuz Corridor Deal
news.body: Brent crude fell roughly 3% to ~$85–86/bbl and WTI slid to ~$80/bbl — the lowest since August 10 — after Iran and Oman jointly announced a 'phased framework' for a temporary joint maritime corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, including a mine-clearing mission. The strait had been effectively closed since the US-Israel war with Iran began in late February 2026, disrupting approximately one-fifth of global seaborne oil and LNG flows. The move came as the US simultaneously pivoted to economic pressure, with Treasury Secretary Bessent pledging a 'zero-leakage' sanctions approach on Iranian oil — measures markets judged as milder than feared. Analysts noted prices are still up over 40% year-to-date, with traders remaining cautious as Iran insisted the strait will only fully reopen when the war ends on all fronts.

news.headline: Copper Hits Record Above $14,400/t; LME Inventories Halved Since May
news.body: Copper futures pushed above $14,400/t — a fresh all-time high — as multiple supply disruptions kept the market acutely tight despite a brief mid-month inventory build. LME-monitored warehouse stocks have fallen by nearly half since mid-May following a 42-day streak of outflows, while SHFE stocks remain depressed. Zijin Mining's half-year report (published August 21) warned that renewed flooding at the Kamoa-Kakula complex in the DRC could cut Zijin's attributable output by up to 57,000 tons this year, threatening its 1.2 million-ton annual target; partner Ivanhoe had already slashed 2026 mine guidance from 380,000–420,000 tons to 290,000–330,000 tons in April. Demand tailwinds from AI data-center buildouts and electrification kept speculative longs extended heading into the week.
news.source: Bloomberg / Mining Weekly / SP Angel / TradingEconomics

news.headline: Coffee Falls >5% as Colombia Earthquake Impact on Buenaventura Port Assessed
news.body: Arabica coffee futures dropped more than 5% — crossing the key market-moving threshold — as traders re-evaluated supply dynamics following a 7.4-magnitude earthquake in Colombia in early August that interrupted operations at Buenaventura, the country's largest coffee export port. Brazil's harvest was running behind schedule at 90% complete versus 97% a year earlier as of mid-August, while ICE-certified arabica inventories fell to a 2.75-year low of 226,242 bags. The selloff appeared partially driven by profit-taking after a prior rally on tight supply; however, ongoing port disruption in Colombia and historically low exchange stocks kept the fundamental backdrop fragile. The next major supply update from Brazil and Colombia is expected to be closely watched for September price direction.
